career_ladder.note: Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates are engaged on a short-term contractual assignment to assist the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India and Judges of the Supreme Court of India in judicial research, special leave petition analysis, and bench briefing under the Scheme for Engaging Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates. While not a permanent civil service cadre, this apex fellowship serves as an elite springboard for Supreme Court advocacy, judicial service appointments, and international postgraduate legal studies.

exam_scheme.note: Selection of Law Clerks is conducted in three comprehensive phases pursuant to the revised Scheme notified by the Supreme Court of India: Phase I Objective Test (CBT), Phase II Subjective Written Test (Research and Case Analysis), and Phase III Oral Interview before Hon'ble Judges.

stages.stage_name: Phase I: Objective Written Test (Computer Based Test)
stages.source_label: Supreme Court of India — Law Clerk Examination Scheme & Guidelines

papers.paper_name: Multiple Choice Questions (Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, Civil Procedure, Evidence Act, Contract Law & Current Legal Developments)
papers.negative_marking: 0.25 marks deducted per wrong answer (25% negative marking)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 50% marks to qualify for evaluation of Phase II

stages.stage_name: Phase II: Subjective Written Examination (Case Analysis & Legal Writing)
stages.source_label: Supreme Court of India — Phase II Written Evaluation Guidelines

papers.paper_name: Part A: Preparation of Case Brief and Bench Memorandum (Analysis of Lower Court / High Court Record)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Evaluated along with Part B for merit shortlisting

papers.paper_name: Part B: Legal Research, Statutory Interpretation & Judgment Synthesis Problem
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 50% aggregate in Phase II for interview consideration

stages.stage_name: Phase III: Oral Interview (Personality & Analytical Assessment)
stages.source_label: Supreme Court of India — Law Clerk Interview Guidelines

papers.paper_name: Personal Interview before the Committee of Hon'ble Supreme Court Judges

financial_package.note: Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates are engaged on a contractual basis and receive a consolidated monthly honorarium of ₹80,000 for the initial assignment period. If extended for a second court year, the honorarium is enhanced to ₹90,000 per month. Being a contractual assignment, it does not carry regular government allowances (DA, HRA, or pension), though comprehensive access to Supreme Court research databases, the Judges Library, and court transit is provided.
financial_package.pay_source_label: Supreme Court of India — Scheme for Engaging Law Clerk-cum-Research Associates Notification (Clause 7)
financial_package.estimate_note: Law Clerks receive a fixed consolidated monthly honorarium of ₹80,000 during their first year, revised to ₹90,000 per month upon approval of extension into the second year. As a contractual engagement under Supreme Court guidelines, standard 7th CPC Dearness Allowance and HRA are not applicable; net in-hand reflects contractual honorarium less applicable professional tax and income tax TDS.
official_perks: Access to Supreme Court Judges Library — the largest judicial research library in Asia
Subscriptions to legal research databases including SCC Online, Manupatra, Westlaw, LexisNexis, and HeinOnline
Direct judicial mentorship and close association with Hon'ble Supreme Court Judges in constitutional and landmark matters
Certificate of Experience issued under the signature of the Registrar, Supreme Court of India
Official ID card granting access to Supreme Court premises, courtrooms, and administrative complexes
Casual leave and medical leave entitlements as specified under Supreme Court clerkship guidelines
